# Issue 007.

The public on-demand rate of AI compute, observed on the August 10 Track 2 priced capture across the locked H100 SXM 80GB-class anchor. United States dollars, per GPU-hour.

...

## A flat priced panel.

All fifteen priced providers were unchanged from Issue 006, producing a zero-movement priced panel in the August 10 observation.

The two repricings recorded in Issue 006 also held again. Hyperstack remained at $3.20 after its move from $2.40, and RunPod Secure Cloud remained at $2.99 after its move from $3.29. On the evidence to date, both changes look persistent rather than like one-cycle anomalies.

The spread remains wide and unchanged from Issue 006: the Tier 1 median of $10.53 is 2.7352 times the pooled non-hyperscaler median used in the Hyperscaler Premium calculation.

## Track 2 under A1-R1.

Issue 007 is a priced-only observation under the two-track cadence adopted August 10 and approved August 11, 2026. The twelve providers excluded at Issue 006 were not recaptured in this Track 2 cycle. Their dispositions carry from the full twenty-seven-provider sweep sealed July 21, and their next full re-verification is due on or about August 21.

The scheduled slots of July 27 and August 3 were not observed. Under A1-R1 the skipped slots force no full sweep and are disclosed here. Movement in Issue 007 is stated against Issue 006.

...

## The current rule.

The SVCI observes public, fixed, on-demand rates for the H100 SXM 80GB-class anchor across a twenty-seven-provider universe in three tiers, from logged-out surfaces only. Quote-gated, from-floor, spot, committed and account-gated figures never enter a median. Full-machine prices divide to per-GPU in recorded arithmetic. Providers without a comparable public rate are excluded and disclosed, not estimated. Under A1-R1, priced-provider observations are captured fresh on weekly or biweekly issue cycles, while the full twenty-seven-provider panel is re-verified on a monthly clock.

results.title: Cheapest H100 and B200 Cloud: CoreWeave vs Nebius vs Lambda vs Crusoe · Aliteq
results.author: Aliteq Team
highlights:
On each provider's own pricing page on Nov 3, 2026, Crusoe had the cheapest on-demand H100 ($3.90 a GPU-hour, rising to $4.50 on Dec 1) and Lambda the cheapest B200 ($6.69). CoreWeave was the most expensive on demand, but its fixed spot prices undercut everyone's on-demand rate. The full table, the catches, and where the marketplace tier sits.

...

## The short answer (read Nov 3, 2026)

Among CoreWeave, Nebius, Lambda and Crusoe, the cheapest on-demand H100 on November 3, 2026 was Crusoe at $3.90 per GPU-hour, then Lambda at $3.99 (8x instance), Nebius at $4.50 and CoreWeave at $6.16 (an 8-GPU node at $49.24 an hour). Crusoe's page says its H100 rises to $4.50 on December 1, 2026. The cheapest on-demand B200 was Lambda at $6.69 per GPU-hour (8x; $6.99 on one GPU), then Nebius at $8.50 and CoreWeave at $8.60; Crusoe's B200 is contact-sales. For interruptible work, CoreWeave's spot nodes work out to $2.46 per H100 and $4.26 per B200, and Nebius preemptible starts from $0.79 (H100) and $0.99 (B200) at a dynamic rate. Smaller clouds go lower still: Hyperstack listed a B200 at $6.00 and an H100 at $2.50.

- Cheapest H100 on demand: Crusoe $3.90 (until Dec 1), Lambda $3.99 (8x), single H100 PCIe at Lambda $3.29
- Cheapest B200 on demand: Lambda $6.69 (8x) to $6.99 (1x)
- Most expensive on demand: CoreWeave, $6.16 per H100 and $8.60 per B200
- Cheapest if you can be interrupted: CoreWeave spot, $2.46 per H100 and $4.26 per B200; Nebius preemptible is dynamic
- Below the big four: Hyperstack B200 $6.00, H100 $2.50; Vast.ai H100 SXM from $2.40

...

- Hyperstack listed on-demand H100 at $2.50 (PCIe), $2.60 (NVLink) and $3.20 (SXM), H200 SXM at $3.99, B200 at $6.00 and B300 at $7.40 per hour on Nov 3, 2026. That B200 price is the lowest data-center on-demand B200 we found on a public price list that day.
- GMI Cloud listed H100 from $2.60 and H200 from $3.20 per GPU-hour; its B200 "from $5.00" is marked contact sales.
- Runpod (Secure Cloud pods) listed H100 PCIe at $2.89, H100 SXM at $3.99, H200 at $5.29 and B200 at $7.99 per hour. The same page's product data also lists Community Cloud rates (B200 $5.98, H100 PCIe $1.99), but its docs say "Runpod is no longer accepting new hosts for Community Cloud. Existing Community Cloud resources remain available," so that capacity is limited to the hosts already there.
- Vast.ai, a marketplace, had H100 SXM from $2.40 and H100 PCIe from $2.54 per hour on demand in our 15:20 UTC read on Nov 3, 2026. Its cheapest on-demand B200 was $10.25, more than any big cloud, so the marketplace isn't the cheap route for Blackwell right now.

...

How we got these numbers

Every big-cloud price is the provider's published rate on its own pricing page, read on Nov 3, 2026, before sales tax, in US dollars. CoreWeave per-GPU figures are its 8-GPU node prices divided by eight (North America). "From" prices are floors, and spot and preemptible prices move. Vast and Runpod prices come from our own price feed (snapshot 15:20 UTC, Nov 3, 2026), which also powers the compare page. A listed price doesn't guarantee capacity. We earn referral fees from Vast and Runpod, not from CoreWeave, Nebius, Lambda, Crusoe, Hyperstack or GMI Cloud, and that doesn't change any number on this page.

results.title: We asked ~50 GPU providers for B300 pricing. Here's the map | TheAI Blog
results.author: Viacheslav Zhvart
highlights:
Published Aug 10, 2026 · updated Nov 5, 2026 · 6 min read

Before we committed to offering GPU capacity ourselves, we did the only sensible thing: we went shopping. Over June and July 2026 we contacted roughly fifty GPU providers — hyperscalers, neoclouds, bare-metal shops, brokers and marketplaces — with the same question every time: "8× B300 nodes, short-to-mid term — what's your price?"

...

## Methodology, briefly

Same ask to everyone: whole nodes of 8× NVIDIA B300 SXM, terms from on-demand to 12 months, US or EU deployment. We collected public pricing pages where they exist, direct quotes where they don't, and marketplace listings where capacity trades openly. Public numbers below are as of July 23, 2026 — this market moves, so treat every figure as a dated snapshot, not gospel. Private quotes are aggregated and anonymized; we don't publish other people's confidential numbers, only the shape they form together.

## The visible market: public on-demand

Only a handful of providers publish an on-demand B300 price at all. As of the snapshot:

| Provider | On-demand, $/GPU·hr |
| --- | --- |
| Hyperstack | $7.40 |
| Verda | $7.50 |
| Nebius | $7.85 |
| AWS (Capacity Blocks) | $14.04 |

Independent price trackers put the market median around $7.85/GPU·hr — up roughly 57% since November. The floor across trackers has hovered in the $6.94–7.39 range for months. That's the market you can see with a browser.

It is worth pausing on the AWS number: a Capacity Block at $14.04 is roughly double the neocloud rate for the same silicon. That premium buys ecosystem integration, not faster matrix multiplies.

...

The subtlest finding, and the one price tables never show: a published on-demand price is not the same thing as an available GPU.

A meaningful share of "on-demand B300" listings today lead to a queue, a "request access" form, or quiet regional stockouts. The price is real; the GPU isn't. You can be looking at a $7+ rate and be unable to deploy at any price — expensive and out of stock at the same time. When you evaluate a provider, the question isn't "what's the number on the page" but "what happens when I click launch."

results.title: The Cloud GPU Price War 2026: Neoclouds vs Hyperscalers
highlights:
Is there a cloud GPU price war in 2026? Yes — but not the one the headlines imply. The real 2026 story is a split market: specialist “neocloud” providers (CoreWeave, Nebius, Lambda, Together AI, RunPod) list on-demand GPUs far below the hyperscalers — a rented H100 starts around $2.89/GPU-hour on a neocloud versus roughly $7–$12/GPU-hour on AWS, Azure, or GCP. Yet reserved, contract, and new Blackwell-generation prices actually rose through the first half of 2026. The war is about who wins list-price comparisons, not about a broad price collapse.

This is a news-analysis of where GPU cloud pricing actually stands in 2026, using only prices verifiable on providers' own pages and figures disclosed in 2026 earnings calls and pricing indices. Where a number can only be sourced to third-party aggregators, it is flagged as such. Last reviewed August 16, 2026.

TL;DR — The 2026 GPU price war in one glance

- Neoclouds list an on-demand H100 from ~$2.89/hr (RunPod) to ~$3.99/hr (Together AI); Nebius lists $3.85/GPU-hr
- Hyperscaler list prices are far higher: AWS p5 works out to ~$6.88/GPU-hr, Azure ND H100 v5 to ~$12.29/GPU-hr (third-party trackers; not confirmed on primary pages)
- One Aug 2026 report puts neocloud rentals up to 66% below the large incumbent clouds
- But contract prices rose: SemiAnalysis' H100 1-year index climbed from ~$1.70 (Oct 2025) toward ~$2.35/GPU-hr (Mar 2026)
- CoreWeave raised list prices ~25% across SKUs in July 2026 and called capacity “effectively sold out”
- AWS quietly raised H200 Capacity Block prices ~15% on Jan 4, 2026 — reportedly its first EC2 GPU price increase in ~two decades
- Nebius disclosed a capacity auction clearing 15% above its highest-ever Blackwell price
- Net: spot/older-Hopper pricing softened; premium, reserved, and Blackwell pricing firmed or rose

...

At the list-price / on-demand tier, specialist clouds genuinely undercut the hyperscalers by a wide margin — and that gap is the marketing engine driving neocloud growth. At the reserved / contract / newest-silicon tier, prices firmed and in several documented cases rose during the first half of 2026, because premium capacity stayed effectively sold out. SemiAnalysis, which publishes a named-methodology H100 rental index, summarizes the tension bluntly: both “GPU prices are falling” and “GPU prices are rising” are true statements in 2026, depending on the tier (SemiAnalysis, 2026).

...

Here is the part that breaks the “prices are crashing” narrative. The single best independent data series on GPU rental pricing — SemiAnalysis' H100 rental index, built from a continuously-collected, composition-resistant weighted mean across hyperscalers, neoclouds, and GPU marketplaces — shows the opposite of a collapse for contract capacity. Its 1-year contract H100 range climbed from roughly $1.70/GPU-hour in October 2025 toward $2.35/GPU-hour by March 2026, with the spot-contract composite index sitting around $2.82/GPU-hour in April 2026 and on-demand capacity marked “sold out” since February (SemiAnalysis H100 index, 2026).

The top of SemiAnalysis' 1-year contract range rose through H1 2026 as premium capacity sold out — the clearest counter-evidence to a broad price war.

...

## The 2026 price hikes nobody announced

If 2026 were a price war, you would expect a run of press-released cuts. Instead, the documented pricing events of 2026 are mostly increases — several delivered quietly.

CoreWeave — ~25% list-price increase across SKUs (July 2026)

On its Q2 2026 earnings call (August 11, 2026), CoreWeave disclosed “an approximately 25% increase across SKUs in response to the current demand environment,” adding that pricing and margins for Blackwell and Vera Rubin SKUs were “setting new highs” while prior-generation SKUs sat at or above prior levels. Management described near-term capacity as “effectively sold out” (CoreWeave Q2 2026 call, via Investing.com). Revenue hit $2.58B, up 112% year over year, on a $104B backlog.

AWS — ~15% H200 Capacity Block increase (Jan 4, 2026)

AWS raised prices on its H200 EC2 Capacity Blocks by roughly 15% effective January 4, 2026 — p5e.48xlarge reportedly moved from $34.61 to $39.80/hr — without a formal customer announcement, in what multiple outlets described as its first EC2 GPU price increase in roughly two decades of EC2 pricing (GIGAZINE, Jan 7, 2026). Treat the exact figures as multiply-reported rather than primary-confirmed.

Nebius — record Blackwell auction clearing price (Q2 2026)

Nebius reported group revenue up more than 450% year over year and a capacity auction clearing 15% above its highest-ever Blackwell price, alongside a swing to positive adjusted EBITDA (Nebius Q2 2026 call, via Investing.com). Not the behavior of a provider slashing prices to win share.
